message.reasoning:
I am reviewing the Monopoly game state to determine my next move.

I have $536 cash and am on VERMONT_AVENUE after paying $400 rent. My pink monopoly is fully developed with four houses each. I hold one get-out-of-jail card. p1 has only $169.

p1 has mortgaged browns and reds, unmortgaged yellows and reds, plus a dark blue monopoly with heavy development. p3 is bankrupt. p4 has $1036 cash and owns Reading RR, light blues fully developed, B&O RR, NC Avenue unmortgaged, and several mortgaged properties. The bank has 12 hotels remaining.

I am deciding what to do after paying rent. I have twelve houses total across my three pink properties. Building a hotel would return four houses to the bank, which p1 could then use. I must avoid selling or hoteling my pink properties.

Boardwalk with four houses pays $1700 in rent. Park Place with three houses pays $1100. Both exceed my $536 cash. I cannot survive a dark blue hit even if I sell all houses, because house sell value is only half their cost.

Selling all twelve houses would yield only $1136 total. That barely covers Park Place but still cannot survive Boardwalk. Unmortgaging either railroad would not complete a set.

I am evaluating trade offers with p1 and p4. All thirty-two houses are currently deployed, so any hotel construction would return houses to the bank. I am calculating exact rent values for my fully developed pink properties.

Four houses on each pink property pay $625, $625, and $700 in rent. Hotels would return four houses to the bank for p1 to use. I will keep my housing lock intact.

p1 cannot build on reds or browns yet because Indiana, Illinois, and Baltic are mortgaged. The unmortgage costs for those properties exceed p1's $169 cash. Pacific is mortgaged too.

p1 cannot build on any set because the bank has no houses to sell. Their only remaining threat is the dark blue monopoly already paying rent. p4 has $1036 and four houses on light blues, so they may try to hotel.

p1 cannot afford a fourth house on Park Place because it costs $200 and they only have $169. A single returned house would still leave them short. However, a yellow house costs $150, so p1 could build one on Atlantic or Ventnor if a house becomes available.

One house on a yellow property pays only about $110, so it poses little threat. The housing lock mainly prevents p1 from completing their dark blue set or building yellows. I am now calculating how dark blue rent will affect my $536 cash.

Boardwalk is a death square. I cannot survive its $1700 rent even after liquidating all twelve houses. Park Place at $1100 would leave me alive with only $36 and no houses, giving p1 the full twelve returned houses to build with.

I am now exploring a trade with p1 to break up their dark blue monopoly. I have no cash to offer, and giving up my pink properties would be too costly. I could offer my get-out-of-jail card instead.

p1 will not trade their dark blue monopoly cheaply. Exchanging my pink properties for theirs is unlikely to succeed. p4 cannot help because I do not own Pacific, and offering my get-out-of-jail card would be useless. I am now considering a direct proposal to p1 that would bring in cash or reduce their threat.

I am now considering buying Park Place or Boardwalk from p1 by offering my pink monopoly plus cash. I need to verify whether buildings transfer with property or must be sold first under these rules. The trade schema only allows cash, properties, and get-out-of-jail cards.

I will avoid trading properties with houses because the engine might reject the offer or force a sell. I am now reconsidering whether to trade at all, since p1 has no cash and p4 still needs Pacific from p1 to complete their green set.

If p1 sells Pacific to p4, p4 still cannot build on greens because the bank has no houses. Hoteling their light blues would free houses but only increases rent by about $100 per property and costs $50 in house price.

Hoteling light blues would free four houses, but that risks giving p1 the tools to build on their dark blue set. I am now weighing four survival paths: avoid landing on dark blues, raise enough cash to survive a hit, break the monopoly through trade, or bankrupt p1 before they can strike. I am calculating whether p1 can afford to hit my pink properties with only $169.

p1 can liquidate seven dark blue houses for roughly $700 and add their $169 cash to about $944 total. That covers the $625 and $700 rent from my pink properties. If they sell those houses, they return to the bank and could rebuild later.

I have four houses on each pink property, so I cannot build more without hoteling. If p1 sells dark blue houses to pay my rent, that weakens their death squares and benefits me. p4 can easily afford light blue rent, but my pink properties hit p1 harder than they would hit p4. I am currently on p4's Vermont Avenue. I will end my turn and avoid unmortgaging or freeing houses.

I am now testing a trade proposal to p1: offer all three pink properties in exchange for Boardwalk and Park Place. This would give me the lethal dark blue monopoly while p1 would receive the pink set.

I am now weighing the house transfer mechanics for that trade. If buildings must be sold first, I would receive only $600 from liquidating my twelve houses, and p1 could rebuild their pink set at roughly $100 per house. That makes the exchange complicated and likely rejected by the engine. Even if buildings transfer freely, swapping twelve houses for seven is a net loss in housing stock. The dark blue set with three or four houses is still stronger than my fully developed pink properties.

I cannot offer p1 enough cash to make a trade with them attractive while keeping myself safe. p4 has no obvious wants, and I have no blocking cards or houses to sell. I am now checking whether p4 might want my Tennessee orange property.

Selling Tennessee would complete p4's orange monopoly, which is too dangerous. The bank currently has no houses available for immediate building. I am now considering offering my mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad to p4; they already own Reading and B&O, so a third would yield only $100 in rent.

I am now considering selling my mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad to p4 for cash. They would pay roughly $50 to $100 to complete their third railroad, and I would gain about $100 in cash. That would raise my total to roughly $636, but I still cannot survive a hit from Boardwalk or Park Place without selling houses. The trade does not improve my survival odds enough to make it worthwhile.

The cash from selling the mortgaged railroad would only save me one house, so the trade is marginal. I am also considering offering my get-out-of-jail card to p1 for cash, but that would not be transformative.

I am now reconsidering whether to build hotels on my three pink properties. Each hotel costs $100 and returns four houses to the bank, but I still cannot survive a hit from Boardwalk or Park Place without selling houses.

Hoteling all three pinks would cost $300 and leave me with $236. p1 could then buy one yellow house for $150, but could not afford a fourth house on Park Place. Hoteling one pink costs $100 and returns four houses. p1 still cannot afford a fourth house on Park Place with only $169. p4 could use the freed houses to hotel their light blues.

I realized that hoteling a property requires four houses already sitting on it, not four houses drawn from the bank. p4 can therefore hotel their light blues immediately without waiting for new houses.

p4 has $1036 and four houses on every light blue property, yet they have not hotelled. Hoteling would free four houses per property and raise rent by $100 each, so their inaction is puzzling.

p4 may be withholding hoteling to keep p1 from buying houses. Hoteling one light blue returns four houses, but p1 still cannot afford a fourth house on Park Place with only $169. Cash is the real constraint, not the bank's house supply.

p1 is $31 short of a fourth house on Park Place. They recently passed GO and collected $200, so they will not pass again for a full lap. I am now checking whether any rent payments could cover that gap.

Even with a rent payment, p1 still cannot afford a fourth house on Park Place because the bank has no houses available. The housing lock remains the real constraint, not cash alone.

I have ruled out hoteling, selling, or unmortgaging as waste of cash. I am now considering buying Pacific from p1 to keep it out of p4's reach permanently.

I am now calculating a $200 offer for Pacific to keep it out of p4's reach. That would leave me with $336 cash and a mortgaged property. p1 would gain $200 and could then afford a fourth house on Park Place if houses are available.

I rejected the $200 offer to p1 because it would fund their Park Place build and waste cash I need to survive. I will not trade with p4 either. Instead, I will use my public message to dissuade p4 from hoteling and p1 from selling Pacific.

I am now drafting a public message to warn p4 against hoteling and p1 against selling Pacific. Hoteling would raise light blue rent by $100, which hurts me after my recent $400 investment. It would also free houses that could eventually help p1 complete Park Place.

I will propose a "housing truce" to p4: neither side will free houses, keeping p1 blocked from building. I must avoid triggering that moment myself. If p1 is forced to sell dark blue houses, the death squares weaken and the race changes.

I am now analyzing the mechanics of a house sale during rent payment. If p1 sells houses to pay me, the returned houses sit in the bank for the next player to claim. p4 already has four houses on every light blue property, so extra houses would not help them build there. Their orange properties are mortgaged, and they lack Tennessee, which is currently mortgaged by me. p1 would also have little cash left after paying rent, so they could not rebuild immediately even if houses were available.

Hoteling my pink properties would return four houses to the bank, but p1 could buy them if they have cash. I am now weighing whether p4 should acquire the green set; without houses available, those properties would remain unbuilt.

Built green monopolies are lethal, so I will keep poisoning that deal. I also refuse to give p4 Tennessee or any orange properties. I am now drafting my end-turn message.

I am weighing whether to be deceptive in my message. I will remind p4 that hoteling light blues only gains $100 rent but hands p1 the houses for Park Place and yellows. I will warn p1 that selling Pacific creates a green monster while their cash is too low to benefit. I am also considering whether to be honest with p4 about the housing truce, since both p1 and p4 are threats.

I am calculating the exact rent I must survive. The game log records $400 paid to p4 on Vermont Avenue, which differs from standard rent. I will trust that log value over standard rules.

I will end the turn. My public message to p4 warns against hoteling light blues because it only raises rent slightly and dumps houses into the bank for p1's Park Place. I will tell p1 that trading Pacific to p4 is a losing deal they cannot afford. I will also state that I am holding onto my houses.

I am now considering trading my get-out-of-jail-free card to p4 for cash. That would be a small gain, but the card is strategically valuable. I might need it later to avoid landing on dark blues or light blues while in jail.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.
